issues.description: Field and related method type inconsistency: The UML in problem_statement.md declares the attribute numberOfInscribedStudents as int (problem_statement.md line 65) and the UML lists getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int (problem_statement.md line 70). The solution implementation declares the field numberOfInscribedStudents as long (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 7) but keeps getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning int (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 75) while its implementation adds numberOfInscribedStudents (long) and numberOfGuestStudents (int) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 76). This mismatch causes a compilation error in the solution code and confuses students about the intended numeric type. The template contains a TODO for adding attributes (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 4) so students have no hint in code which type to choose.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the numeric type consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution to declare numberOfInscribedStudents as int (replace 'private long numberOfInscribedStudents;' with 'private int numberOfInscribedStudents;'), update the constructor parameter and getter/setter to use int, and keep getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning int (ensuring the addition is int + int). Alternative: if large counts are intended, update the UML and problem statement to declare numberOfInscribedStudents as long and change getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return long (and update template/comments accordingly). Document the chosen option in the problem statement so students know which numeric type to implement.
